subject: Government
title: The Civil Service and Public Administration
outline: Meaning of civil service and public service
Structure and hierarchy of the civil service
The Civil Service Commission and recruitment
Problems of the Nigerian civil service and reforms

modules.title: Nature, Structure and Features
modules.html:
1. Meaning

The civil service is the body of permanent, paid officials employed in the civil capacity of the state to advise on and implement government policy in ministries, departments and extra-ministerial agencies. The wider public service includes the civil service plus the police, armed forces, judiciary staff, public corporations, universities and local government employees.

2. Structure of a Ministry

LevelOfficerRole
Political headMinister / CommissionerPolicy direction and political responsibility
Administrative headPermanent Secretary / Director-GeneralChief adviser and accounting officer of the ministry
DirectorateDirectors and Deputy DirectorsHead departments and divisions
MiddleAssistant Directors, Chief and Principal OfficersBranches and sections
JuniorExecutive, clerical and support staffRoutine implementation

The service is grouped into classes: administrative, professional, executive, clerical and manipulative/auxiliary.

3. Features

  1. Permanence — officials remain when governments change.
  2. Neutrality — they serve any government of the day without partisanship.
  3. Anonymity — they act in the minister's name; the minister answers publicly.
  4. Impartiality — decisions follow rules, not personal or ethnic favour.
  5. Hierarchy — clear chain of command and channels of communication.
  6. Expertise and professionalism — recruitment by merit and competitive examination.
  7. Official secrecy — bound by the Official Secrets Act and oath.

4. Weber's Bureaucracy

Max Weber's ideal type of bureaucracy features hierarchy of offices, division of labour by specialisation, written rules and records, impersonality, recruitment and promotion by merit, and a career structure with fixed salaries. It maximises efficiency but risks red tape, rigidity and goal displacement, where rules become ends in themselves.

examples.q: A ministry is criticised in the National Assembly for a failed contract. Who answers and why?
examples.a: The Minister answers, under the doctrine of ministerial responsibility, because civil servants act anonymously in his name. Internally the Permanent Secretary, as accounting officer, bears responsibility for financial regularity and may be queried, disciplined or invited by the Public Accounts Committee, but publicly and politically the minister carries the blame.

examples.q: Why must the civil service be politically neutral?
examples.a: Because governments change but administration must continue. Neutrality ensures continuity of policy implementation, protects officials from dismissal on partisan grounds, guarantees that the incoming government inherits trustworthy advisers, and preserves public confidence that state resources are not used for party advantage.

modules.title: Functions, Commissions, Problems and Reform
modules.html:
1. Functions of the Civil Service

  1. Advising ministers on policy formulation.
  2. Implementing and administering approved policies and laws.
  3. Providing continuity and institutional memory.
  4. Delegated legislation: drafting rules and regulations.
  5. Quasi-judicial functions through tribunals and disciplinary panels.
  6. Collection of revenue and management of public finance.
  7. Delivery of public services and record keeping.
  8. Representing government in negotiations and international meetings.

2. The Federal Civil Service Commission

Established under section 153 of the 1999 Constitution, it appoints, promotes, transfers and disciplines civil servants (other than those in offices reserved to other bodies), insulating recruitment from political interference and applying the federal character principle.

3. Problems of the Nigerian Civil Service

ProblemEffect
Corruption and briberyInflated contracts, ghost workers, loss of revenue
Red tape and excessive procedureDelay in service delivery
Political interferenceErosion of neutrality and merit
Poor remuneration and welfareLow morale, brain drain, moonlighting
Overstaffing at junior levels, shortage of specialistsHigh wage bill, weak technical capacity
Nepotism and quota abuseMediocre appointments
Obsolete equipment and poor recordsInefficiency and lost files

4. Reform Efforts

  • Udoji Commission (1972–1974) — unified grading and salary structure, management by objectives.
  • Dotun Phillips Panel (1985) and the 1988 Civil Service Reorganisation Decree — made ministers chief executives and professionalised ministries; largely reversed in 1995 on the Ayida Panel's advice.
  • Ayida Review Panel (1994–1995) — restored the office of Permanent Secretary and the pool system.
  • Modern measures: monetisation of benefits, IPPIS payroll and BVN verification to remove ghost workers, e-governance, due process/BPP procurement reform, treasury single account, SERVICOM service charters, and performance-based promotion.

examples.q: Evaluate the impact of the 1988 civil service reform.
examples.a: It made the Minister both chief executive and accounting officer, abolished the pool system so that officers made careers within one ministry, and created professionalised directorates. Intended benefits were specialisation and clearer responsibility. In practice it politicised administration, eroded the neutrality and anonymity of career officers, weakened financial control and blurred the adviser–decider distinction, so the Ayida Panel recommended restoration of the Permanent Secretary system in 1995.

examples.q: How does the IPPIS reduce payroll fraud?
examples.a: The Integrated Personnel and Payroll Information System centralises staff records and pays salaries directly from a single database linked to Bank Verification Numbers. Duplicate and fictitious 'ghost workers' cannot survive biometric verification, and ministries lose the discretion to inflate nominal rolls, thereby cutting recurrent expenditure and improving transparency.

modules.title: Meaning of civil service and public service
modules.html:
Meaning of civil service and public service is a key part of The Civil Service and Public Administration (SSS 2, Government). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Meaning The civil service is the body of permanent, paid officials employed in the civil capacity of the state to advise on and implement government policy in ministries, departments and extra-ministerial agencies.
  • The wider public service includes the civil service plus the police, armed forces, judiciary staff, public corporations, universities and local government employees.
  • Structure of a Ministry Level Officer Role Political head Minister / Commissioner Policy direction and political responsibility Administrative head Permanent Secretary / Director-General Chief adviser and accounting officer of the ministry Directorate Directors and Deputy Directors Head departments and divisions Middle Assistant Directors, Chief and Principal Officers Branches and sections Junior Executive, clerical and support staff Routine implementation The service is grouped into classes : administrative, professional, executive, clerical and manipulative/auxiliary.
  • Anonymity — they act in the minister's name; the minister answers publicly.
  • Functions of the Civil Service Advising ministers on policy formulation.

Worked example

Q: Civil servants remain in office when governments change because of:
A: Permanence — Permanence guarantees continuity of administration.

Q: The doctrine that a minister answers publicly for his ministry is:
A: Ministerial responsibility — Ministerial responsibility complements civil-service anonymity.

examples.q: Civil servants remain in office when governments change because of:
examples.a: Permanence — Permanence guarantees continuity of administration.

examples.q: The doctrine that a minister answers publicly for his ministry is:
examples.a: Ministerial responsibility — Ministerial responsibility complements civil-service anonymity.

modules.title: Bureaucracy after Max Weber

Key points

  • Weber's Bureaucracy Max Weber's ideal type of bureaucracy features hierarchy of offices, division of labour by specialisation, written rules and records, impersonality, recruitment and promotion by merit, and a career structure with fixed salaries.
  • It maximises efficiency but risks red tape , rigidity and goal displacement, where rules become ends in themselves.

Worked example

Q: Weber's bureaucracy emphasises:
A: Hierarchy, rules and merit — The ideal type stresses hierarchy, written rules, impersonality and merit recruitment.

examples.a: Hierarchy, rules and merit — The ideal type stresses hierarchy, written rules, impersonality and merit recruitment.

quiz.q: The administrative head of a Nigerian federal ministry is the:
quiz.solution: The Permanent Secretary is the career head and accounting officer of the ministry.

quiz.q: Civil servants remain in office when governments change because of:
quiz.solution: Permanence guarantees continuity of administration.

quiz.q: The doctrine that a minister answers publicly for his ministry is:
quiz.solution: Ministerial responsibility complements civil-service anonymity.

quiz.q: Recruitment into the federal civil service is handled by the:
quiz.solution: Section 153 establishes the Commission to appoint, promote and discipline officers.

quiz.q: The Udoji Commission reported in:
quiz.solution: The Udoji Public Service Review Commission reported in 1974, introducing a unified grading structure.

quiz.q: Excessive adherence to rules and procedures is called:
quiz.solution: Red tape is bureaucratic delay caused by procedural rigidity.

quiz.q: Weber's bureaucracy emphasises:
quiz.solution: The ideal type stresses hierarchy, written rules, impersonality and merit recruitment.

quiz.q: Which is NOT part of the civil service proper?
quiz.solution: Soldiers belong to the wider public service but not the civil service, which is civil in character.

quiz.q: The 1988 reform made the chief executive of a ministry the:
quiz.solution: The reform designated the Minister as chief executive and accounting officer.

quiz.q: The Ayida Panel of 1994/95 recommended:
options: Restoration of the Permanent Secretary system
quiz.solution: It reversed key 1988 changes and restored the traditional career structure.

quiz.q: Payment of salaries through a central biometric database is achieved by:
quiz.solution: IPPIS centralises personnel and payroll data to eliminate ghost workers.

quiz.q: Anonymity of civil servants means they:
options: Work without public credit or blame
quiz.solution: They act in the minister's name and are shielded from public accountability.

quiz.q: Which class of the civil service handles routine record keeping?
quiz.solution: The clerical class performs routine documentation and record duties.

quiz.q: Drafting of subsidiary rules under an Act is:
quiz.solution: Officials make regulations under powers delegated by the legislature.

quiz.q: A key cause of low morale in the Nigerian civil service is:
quiz.solution: Inadequate pay and welfare drive brain drain and corruption.

quiz.q: SERVICOM was introduced to:
quiz.solution: SERVICOM sets service charters and standards for public agencies.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a function of the Civil Service Commission?
options: Recruitment and promotion of civil servants
quiz.solution: The Commission is an independent body that ensures merit-based recruitment, promotion, and discipline of government employees.

quiz.q: The Civil Service is permanent because:
options: Governments come and go, but they remain
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Governments come and go, but they remain.

quiz.q: The primary function of the Civil Service is to...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Formulate and implement government policies.

quiz.q: The Civil Service is characterized by:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Anonymity/Neutrality.

quiz.q: Public corporations are managed by _____.
quiz.solution: Public corporations (like NNPC) are typically governed by a Board of Directors appointed by the government to oversee operations.

quiz.q: Public opinion is mainly measured through:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Elections/Polls.

quiz.q: Public corporations are established mainly to:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Provide essential services.

quiz.q: Public opinion is measured through:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Elections and Polls.

quiz.q: Public Corporations are established primarily to...
options: Provide essential services to the public
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Provide essential services to the public.

quiz.q: The Civil War ended in:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: 1970.

quiz.q: Public opinion is measured by:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Mass Media/Polls.

quiz.q: Public opinion is mainly formed through:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: The Mass Media.

quiz.q: The ‘Vassalage’ system was most common in which pre-colonial administration?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Hausa/Fulani.

quiz.q: What is ‘Public Opinion’?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Collective views of the people.

quiz.q: The 'Willink Commission' of 1957 was set up to _____.
quiz.solution: The commission was established to investigate the fears of minority groups in Nigeria and suggest safeguards for their rights.

quiz.q: Bureaucracy is a term associated with...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: The civil service.

quiz.q: A core feature of Bureaucracy is?
options: High speed and lack of records
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Hierarchy and adherence to rules.

quiz.q: Who headed the 1957 commission into the fears of minorities in Nigeria?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Henry Willink.

quiz.q: The ‘Willink Commission’ was set up in 1957 to?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Allay the fears of minorities.

quiz.q: What is ‘Bureaucracy’?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Rule by officials and administrators.

quiz.q: The term of office for the Secretary-General of the United Nations is _____ years.
quiz.solution: The UN Secretary-General is appointed for a 5-year term, which is renewable.

quiz.q: Universal Adult Suffrage refers to the _____.
options: Right of all adults to bear arms
Right of all adults to vote
Right of all adults to free education
Right of all adults to travel
quiz.solution: Suffrage is the right to vote. Universal adult suffrage means all qualified adults can vote regardless of property, gender, or social status.

quiz.q: The organ of the United Nations responsible for maintaining global peace and security is the _____.
quiz.solution: The Security Council has the primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security.

quiz.q: Gerrymandering refers to the _____.
quiz.solution: Gerrymandering is the practice of redrawing the borders of an electoral district to favor one political party over another.

quiz.q: The headquarters of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is in _____.
quiz.solution: Abuja, Nigeria, serves as the administrative headquarters for the ECOWAS commission.

quiz.q: Non-alignment as a foreign policy principle means _____.
options: Not taking sides in the Cold War
quiz.solution: Non-alignment was a policy where developing nations chose not to be formally aligned with either the USA-led or USSR-led blocs during the Cold War.

quiz.q: The first President of the Organization of African Unity (OAU) was _____.
quiz.solution: Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia served as the first chairperson of the OAU in 1963.

quiz.q: The main objective of pressure groups is to _____.
options: Protect the interest of their members
quiz.solution: Pressure groups (like ASUU or NLC) exist primarily to advocate for and protect the specific interests of their members.

quiz.q: Which organization replaced the League of Nations?
quiz.solution: The United Nations was established in 1945 to replace the League of Nations which had failed to prevent World War II.

quiz.q: The 'Age Grade' system was a significant feature of pre-colonial _____ politics.
quiz.solution: In decentralized Igbo societies, age grades performed various social, executive, and military duties.

quiz.q: ECOWAS was established to promote:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Economic integration.

quiz.q: The primary function of the Judiciary is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Interpretation of law.

quiz.q: The NCNC was led by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Herbert Macaulay/Azikiwe.

quiz.q: A referendum is used to:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Decide on a public issue.
